note: Real parsed data (data/parsed/earth_sites_criteria.csv). Missing criteria are null; the scorer skips them.

sites.name: Yungay, Atacama Desert
sites.description: The driest non-polar desert on Earth. Hyper-arid soils, nitrate and perchlorate salts and extreme UV make it a classic analog for Martian soil chemistry and life detection.

sites.name: Wright Valley, McMurdo Dry Valleys
sites.description: Ice-free polar desert with katabatic winds, sublimating ground ice, polygonal terrain and briny ponds. One of the closest climate analogs to Mars.

sites.name: Don Juan Pond
sites.description: A calcium-chloride brine pond that stays liquid down to about −50 °C. Water tracks feeding it are a model for deliquescence-driven brines on Mars.

sites.name: Haughton Crater, Devon Island
sites.description: A 23 km impact crater in a polar desert. Home of the NASA Haughton-Mars Project for testing rovers, suits and field operations.

sites.name: Río Tinto
sites.description: Acidic, iron-rich river with jarosite and other sulfates that mirror the sulfate deposits seen at Meridiani Planum.

sites.name: Mauna Kea summit
sites.description: High-altitude basaltic volcano with palagonitic, Mars-like regolith, strong UV and thin air. Used for in-situ resource utilization (ISRU) and rover tests.

sites.name: Kaʻū Desert, Kīlauea
sites.description: Basaltic tephra plains, fresh lava flows and skylit lava tubes. A strong analog for volcanic terrain and caves on Mars.

sites.name: Holuhraun lava field
sites.description: One of the youngest flood basalts on Earth, with glacial outwash and black basaltic sand dunes, much like Martian volcanic plains.

sites.name: Bockfjord Volcanic Complex, Svalbard
sites.description: Arctic volcanic center with carbonate globules similar to those in Martian meteorite ALH84001. Used as an AMASE test site.

sites.name: Mars Desert Research Station, Hanksville
sites.description: Red Jurassic mudstones, clays and gypsum near the Mars Society habitat used for long-duration crew simulations.

sites.name: Kelso Dunes, Mojave Desert
sites.description: Tall booming sand dunes and desert pavement. Used to test rover traction and dune morphology.

sites.name: Badwater Basin, Death Valley
sites.description: Salt pans, evaporites and extreme heat below sea level, with Mars Hill and ancient lake beds nearby.

sites.name: Sossusvlei, Namib Desert
sites.description: Giant star and linear dunes with fog-fed moisture, comparable to the large Martian dune fields.

sites.name: Timanfaya, Lanzarote
sites.description: Barren basaltic lava fields, cinder cones and lava tubes. Used by the ESA PANGAEA geology training course.

sites.name: Dresser Formation, Pilbara
sites.description: 3.5 billion-year-old stromatolites and hydrothermal silica: a reference for searching ancient Martian rocks for biosignatures.

sites.name: Lonar Crater
sites.description: A young impact crater in Deccan basalt with a saline, alkaline lake. A rare basalt-hosted impact analog.

sites.name: Dallol, Danakil Depression
sites.description: Hyper-acidic, hypersaline hydrothermal field with sulfur, iron oxides and potash salts. An extreme habitability test bed.

sites.name: Dalangtan Playa, Qaidam Basin
sites.description: High, cold, hyper-arid playa with chlorides, sulfates and wind-carved yardangs, very similar to Martian evaporite basins.

sites.name: Lava Beds National Monument
sites.description: More than 700 lava tube caves with ice deposits and skylights. Used for cave robotics and subsurface life detection.

sites.name: Craters of the Moon
sites.description: Basaltic fissure eruptions, spatter cones and lava tubes. Used in NASA's FINESSE and BASALT field campaigns.

sites.name: Lost Hammer Spring, Axel Heiberg Island
sites.description: Perennial sub-zero hypersaline spring flowing through permafrost, an analog for brines and methane seeps on Mars.

sites.name: Salar de Uyuni
sites.description: The world's largest salt flat, at 3,650 m. Evaporite crusts, high UV and polygonal salt ridges.

sites.name: White Sands
sites.description: Gypsum dune field, the largest on Earth, analogous to the sulfate-rich dunes around the Martian north pole.

sites.name: Tolbachik volcano, Kamchatka
sites.description: Active basaltic volcano with fumarolic minerals, lava tubes and snowfields. A cold volcanic analog.

sites.name: Wadi Rum
sites.description: Red sandstone desert used as a Mars film set and for Austrian Space Forum (ÖWF) AMADEE analog missions.

sites.name: Dasht-e Lut yardangs
sites.description: Among the hottest surfaces on Earth, with giant wind-sculpted yardangs like those of the Medusae Fossae Formation.

sites.name: Las Cañadas del Teide, Tenerife
sites.description: High volcanic caldera used to test ExoMars instruments, with basaltic and phonolitic lavas and clear, high-UV skies.

sites.name: Pinacate Peaks
sites.description: Maar craters, cinder cones and lava fields bordering the Gran Desierto dune sea. Apollo astronauts trained here.

sites.name: Erg Chebbi, Sahara
sites.description: Star dunes beside hamada plains and evaporites. Used for ESA and Mars rover field testing.

sites.name: Utqiaġvik polygon tundra
sites.description: Ice-wedge polygons on continuous permafrost that closely resemble the patterned ground at the Phoenix landing site.
